This is in response to several separate enquiries you have made relating to spouse, partner, and/or dependent child sponsorships.

1. We continue to receive feedback from those who are unsuccessful and to use this information to help identify ways to improve the process. As you are aware, linking an application to an online account – while it has benefits for clients-is not mandatory.
2. Have you considered having fewer match points, to decrease the chance of error? ### Subject:Start-Up Visa Program-Business Incubators-REP-2017-1578

Importance:High

##### Dear Ms.

Thank you for contacting the Immigration Representatives mailbox. We trust that you will find the answer to your question below of assistance.

##### Question #1:

I note that the attached indicates in multiple places that the business incubator must confirm that it has performed due diligence on various requirements including control over any intellectual property or other assets that they are bringing to the business, the applicant, business and investment. What exactly would be required of the business in this regard?

##### Response #1:

Applicants (Businesses) must meet the following requirements to be found eligible under the Start-up Visa program:

have a Letter of Support from a designated angel investor group, venture capital fund or business incubator meet the ownership requirements for a qualifying business get scores of at least Canadian Language Benchmark (CLB) 5 in all four categories for either English or French, and have an adequate amount of money to settle and provide for the cost of living prior to earning an income.

Designated entities are required to perform a due diligence assessment of the applicants and the applicants' business in accordance with industry standards. IRCC provides business incubators essential information that should be included on the term sheet/client agreement and the commitment certificate. This will assist officers in assessing whether or not sufficient due diligence has been performed on an application under the Start-up visa program. However, IRCC looks to the industry associations to advise on what is standard for the industry and whether those standards have been met. In cases where the visa officers have questions about the due diligence performed by a designated entity, or on a random basis (for quality assurance), the visa officers may send the case to the industry association to conduct a peer review. A peer review is an independent assessment of a commitment by a panel of experts convened by the industry

#### association that represents the lead designated entity on the Commitment Certificate. The peer review

process was designed to build in safeguards to protect against fraud and to ensure that the deals made between private sector partners and foreign entrepreneurs are in accordance with industry standards. Section 11 of the Ministerial Instructions outline the grounds for review and the need for an independent assessment or peer review.

##### Question # 2:

What is the risk to a business incubator with respect to the commitments that it is making to supporting a new start up business under this program if for example the due diligence was found inadequate and the application was

## unsuccessful? Is there a guide for Business Incubators to refer to?

### Response# 2:

- If, at the end of their determination, the visa officers are not satisfied that the designated entity performed sufficient due diligence, the applicants' permanent resident applications can be refused. This is stated under section 9 of the Ministerial Instructions: 9(2) If the officer is not satisfied that the entity assessed the applicant and the applicant's business in a manner consistent with industry standards or that the terms of the commitment are consistent with industry standards, the officer may refuse to issue the permanent resident visa. We hope this information will assist you.

# Start-Up Visa: Peer Reviews Start-Up Visa: Peer Reviews

Nm Immigration,

What is a peer review? A peer review is an independent assessment of a commitment by a panel of experts convened by the industry association that represents the lead designated entity on the Commitment Certificate. For example, if the Commitment Certificate was issued by a designated angel investor group. then the National Angel Capital Organization is responsible for organizing a peer review panel to evaluate the commitment. The peer review process was designed to build in safeguards to protect against fraud and to ensure that the deals made between private-sector partners and foreign entrepreneurs are in accordance with industry standards.

When must a peer review be done?

The peer review process must be initiated:

when the visa officer has concerns about the Commitment Certificate and/or whether the designated entity has performed due diligence according to industry standards; and for quality assurance on a random basis.

### Who initiates peer reviews?

All peer reviews are initiated by a visa officer at Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). The visa officer will complete the Peer Review Request form (IMM 5765) and send it to the industry association naned in the application. The industry association must then assemble a panel of experts within four weeks.

Immigration, Relugees Imnmigranon, Retuges and Cazseship Canada et Caoyenneia Canada 1+1

tCitizenshipCanada

What is provided to the panel? The visa officer will provide the panel with the following:

the Commitment Certificate: the term sheet/client agreement: and other relevant supporting documentation.

What is the role of the panel?

The peer review panel must request a copy of the due diligence package from the designated entity. At that time, the panel should also advise the designated entity of the date of the peer review. so that a representative froni the designated entity is available to answer questions via teleconference if needed.

The panel members must not disclose any information that they receive about an applicant's business during the peer review process.

### What does the panel assess?

The panel will review the due diligence package to assess whether the designated entity undertook the required due diligence in accordance with industry standards outlined as follows:

1. Are the business model and value proposition, as well as the sources of actual and projected revenues, clearly articulated? Has a suffictent level of due diligence been performed to demonstrate that this is à growth- oriented business that is viable in Canada?
### What does the panel assess (cont’)?

2.Has a current list of shareholders been provided and has the due diligence process reviewed the shareholder agreements?
3.Has the due diligence process properly covered the business' overall marketing, sales and distribution strategy?
4. Has the due diligence process reviewed the business relevant material contracts in key areas such as sales. distribution and marketing employment agreements with executive officers and loan agreements with officers, directors and holders of > 5% of the shares?
5. Has the due diligence process adequately reviewed the control that the business has over the intellectual property and other assets that it needs to operate cuccessfully?
6.Has the due diligence process adequately reviewed the audited financial statements and notes, the quarterly financial statements and the capital budget for the current and next fiscal year?
7. Has the due diligence process adequately reviewed all the agreements relative to obligations for borrowed money, copies of all binding agreements, and the projected use of proceeds from the current financing round?
8. Has the due diligence process adequately reviewed all material employment and consulting agreements as well as stock options, bonus structures, retirement plans, profit-sharing, incentives and pension plan details?
9. Has the required due diligence on the management team been performed inmsgration, Retugees Iemgaton, Retugiés and Cazmesnp Canada A Caoyerrste Canada
and did it properly assess the team's ability to successfully build and grow the business in Canada?

10. Any other due diligence completed or an explanation for why the above was not completed, if applicable. What does the panel do when they
complete their assessment?

If the peer review panel has any doubts or concerns regarding the due diligence undertaken by a designated entity, the panel should address these with à representative from the designated entity and provide them with an opportunity to respond verbally.

After this discussion. should the peer review panel still find that the designated entity has not conducted sufficient due diligence or has not operated in accordance with industry standards in any of the above areas, the panel should advise the designated entity so that they understand what the problems were and what they must do differently in the future. The peer review findíngs must also be returned to [RCC via secure e-mail (Entrust) or by courier.

During this process, the panelists identites must not be disclosed to the designated entity or the applicants. What is the role of the visa officer?

Visa officers will consider the assessment provided by the peer review panel. However, they are not constrained by it in making a final decision. They will stiíl assess all information and make a decision based on their own findings. Authority to make a final decision on the case rests with the visa officer.

#### Citizenship and Citoyenneté et INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE WITH FORM IMM 5766E

Immigration Canada Immigration Canada

#### PROTECTED WHEN COMPLETED-B

## START-UP BUSINESS CLASS COMMITMENT CERTIFICATE FOR DESIGNATED ENTITIES

INSTRUCTIONS

1.0 Designated Entity Information This section must be completed by the lead designated entity.
1.1 Name of the designated entity You must write the complete name of your designated entity here as it appears in the Ministerial Instructions Schedules 1, 2 or 3.
1.2 Type of designated entity You_must select the type of designated entity from the drop-down menu. The choices are NACO for an angel investor group, CVCA for a venture capital fund or CABI for a business incubator.
2.0 Applicant Information
2.1 Name of the primary applicant It is important that this section accurately reflect the applicant's name as it appears on their passport or travel documents, as well as any other names by which this person is known. For example Mitch Soon is the name that you call this person. However, you are aware and have confirmed that his official name is Myasong SoonLi. In this instance you must include Myasong SoonLi in the sections entitled Family Name and Given name(s) and Mitch Soon in the section entitled Other name(s).
2.4 Is this person essential to the business? You must indicate whether or not this person is essential to the business. If you would not be willing to invest in this business without this person, then this person should be identified as essential on this Commitment Certificate.
Note: If the application of a person identified as essential is refused or withdrawn, all other team members will be refused.

2.5 Mailing address You must indicate the mailing address for the primary applicant. The address indicated in this area will be transposed to the Letter of Support which will be printed at the end of this document.
3.0 Members of the Entrepreneur Team (who are not Canadian Citizens or Permanent Residents) Refers to the other members of the entrepreneurial team that you are investing in, who are applying for visas on the basis of the same commitment. You must identify all members of the entrepreneurial team in this section, ensuring each applicant's name reflects what appears on their passport or travel documents. If the person that you identify is essential to the business, select “yes".
Note: Although you must identify all team members in this section, only one Commitment Certificate is required for the entrepreneurial team. However, each individual must receive a
 copy of the Letter of Support. The Commitment Certificate must be approved by an authorized representative of the designated entity. The agreement details are outlined in a document called a term sheet or client agreement which must be sent electronically to CiC along with the Commitment Certificate.
4.0 Business Structure
4.1 Control of intellectual property or other business assets The applicants must have control over any intellectual property or other assets that they are bringing to the business (if applicable). You must confirm that you have performed due diligence, including source of funds on this requirement. Select "yes" or “no".
4.2 Financial, legal structure and incorporation of the business Describe the financial and legal structure of the business, including details related to incorporation or plans to incorporate. This section must clearly detail everyone who holds an interest (voting rights attached to shares) in the business.
- Who has voting rights in this business?
- What percentage of voting rights belong to the applicant?
- What other people or entities hold voting rights?

In addition, in order for the applicant to be considered for a work permit, the following parameters must be met:
- The applicant must intend to reside in a province or territory other than Quebec;
- A Commitment Certificate/Letter of Support must have been issued by you, the designated entity, indicating that the work permit applicant is “essential" and that there are urgent business reasons for the individual's early entry to Canada (i.e. section 8.0 of the Commitment Certificate is completed);

## 8.3 Proof of funds / Financial support

CIC will assess the applicant's financial sufficiency according to the applicant's family size, using the current Low Income Cut-off (LICO) from Statistics Canada for a 52-week period. You must indicate that your organization has confirmed that the applicant has sufficient financiaǐ resources to support themselves and their dependants during the 52-week period for which a work permit is sought. Select "yes" or "no". The funds must be available and transferable, and unencumbered by debts or other obligations, in order to demonstrate the applicant's financial sufficiency. Monies that have been provided to the applicant by your organization could be included in this assessment, if they have been provided to the applicant to cover living expenses and are not related to launching or running the new business in Canada. A recent bank statement or other financial document or instrument and a signed statement from the applicant, indicating that the funds are available, unencumbered by debts or other obligations, and are transferable to Canada, is sufficient.

## Dear

Thank you for your email correspondence to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's Immigration Representatives mailbox.

Please note that our calculation is based on monthly units, and we do not take into account days. When inputting work experience "From and To" dates, the system only asks for month and year for each entry. The date range is inclusive, meaning the month in the "To" date will count towards the calculation of full time equivalent units for that particular work experience entry. Example: Using the February 1st date, and assuming the candidate worked for a year (full-time and met relevant definition of work experience), the calculation would be as follows depending on whether To Date is set to January or

# February:

February 2015- January 2016 = 12 months full-time equivalent duration; February 2015- February 2016= 13 months full-time equivalent duration

In a case such as your client's, at time of assessment, the IRCC reviewing officer will use their discretion when evaluating information and supporting documents included in the application. If your client meets all other minimum requirements and the applicant indicated that the job is ongoing and they would meet work experience in the short interim, the officer may consider that this meets the work experience requirement. However, if your client prefers to be sure of the outcome s/he may decline this round of invitations and wait for future rounds once the work experience meets CEC requirement.

We trust this information will assist you.

# Sincerely,

#### The Immigration Representatives Mailbox

We regret that you are experiencing technical issues uploading Schedule As using the representative portal.

Schedule As can be submitted without an ink signature through the Client or Representative Portals because -- when any document is submitted this way-there is an additional electronic signature process built into the portal, which is linked to a credential such as an individual's GCKey. Documents submitted through our Web Form require an ink signature because a submission through the web form does not involve providing the same kind of secure electronic signature.

We do not normally deal with case specific issues through this mailbox. However, if you would be willing to provide one or two application numbers as examples, we can look into what may be causing your difficulty.

Wednesdav. Mav 17. 2017 11:05 AM Sent: To: Subject:FW: Appeal allowed at IAD-Procedure on what happens next at visa post-REP-2016-1899-

### due by Jan. 11

Importance:High

Good day,

Thank you for your questions, apologies for the delayed response

You have submitted two inquiries with similar questions. One in December 2016 below, and one in February 2017. reference number REP-2017-0283. It was responded to with the following information, which answers both inquiries:

What is the procedure, for a permanent resident of Canada who won their appeal at IAD on Residency Obligation (for a PR applied for PRTD and was found by the Visa office not to have met the Residency obligation, but the decision of officer was set aside by the lAD).

Will the Visa office continue to process the PRTD? In a situation where the Immigration Appeal Division (lAD) of the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB) allows an appeal of a negative residency determination decision made outside of Canada, the lAD sets aside the original decision and as per subsection 67(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and will "substitute a determination that, in its opinion, should have been made, including the making of a removal order, or refer the matter to the appropriate decision-maker for reconsideration." Where an appeal of a negative residency determination is allowed, the CBSA will inform IRCC of the IAD decision so that IRCC may take the necessary steps which will depend on the specific decision made by the lAD. The client would not need to make a new PRTD application as the original application would continue to be processed. The client may, however, wish to provide the notice they received from the lAD that the appeal was allowed to the processing office. Contact information for IRCC can be found on the IRCC website at [http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/offices/index.asp](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/offices/index.asp).

How long after the IAD decision will they process the PRTD? Is there a time limit before the visa office must process the PRTD? What is the procedure or recourse does the PR have, if the Visa office does not continue to process the PRTD in the specified time period? There is no specific timeframe for the office to complete the processing of the PRTD application following the lAD's decision; however, as soon as IRCC receives notification of the lAD decision, they will process the request as quickly as possible. Should the client wish to do so, they may also provide the notice they received from the lAD that the appeal was allowed to the processing office. If the application is taking longer than expected or the client needs to contact IRCC for any other reason regarding their PRTD application, they may contact the office processing their application. Contact information for IRCC can be found on the IRCC website at [http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/offices/index.asp](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/offices/index.asp).

# Regards,

Your portal account is personal and should transfer with you to your new firm. As you state, the first step in this process would be to have your existing clients sign a new "use of representative” form IMM5476 with a different lawyer at your current firm, and upload these forms through the case enquiry web form indicating a change of representative.

Upon submission of change of representatives, the new representative or lawyer will have to link to each client's file via their portal, subsequently removing the file from your portal account.
